questions.text: Who counts as an entrepreneur under the UGB?
options: Only someone who owns a GmbH or AG
Anyone who runs a business alone or with others
Only someone who runs a business for profit
Only someone registered in the commercial register
questions.correctAnswer: Anyone who runs a business alone or with others

questions.text: When does an entrepreneur have a registered business name (Firma)?
options: Only after entry in the commercial register
As soon as a trading name is chosen
As soon as a trade is registered
questions.correctAnswer: Only after entry in the commercial register

questions.text: What makes up a business name?
Which rule bans a name that misleads people about the actual business?
Where are key business details such as legal form and register number recorded?
When must a sole trader register because of turnover?
options: Above EUR 1 million in one year or above EUR 700,000 in each of two consecutive years
At EUR 1 million in two consecutive years or above EUR 700,000 in total
Above EUR 700,000 in one year or above EUR 1 million combined over two years
questions.correctAnswer: Above EUR 1 million in one year or above EUR 700,000 in each of two consecutive years

questions.text: Which legal form must be registered regardless of turnover?
A GmbH must keep double-entry accounts even with very low turnover.
For the EUR 700,000 turnover threshold, it is enough for the two years combined to exceed that amount.
A sole trader has turnover of EUR 820,000 and then EUR 730,000 in two consecutive years. Is registration compulsory? Briefly explain.
questions.correctAnswer: Compulsory: each of the two consecutive financial years is above EUR 700,000.

questions.text: How many owners does a sole proprietorship have?
options: At least one general and one limited partner

questions.text: How is a sole proprietorship established?
What statutory minimum capital does a sole proprietorship require?
How is a sole trader liable for business debts?
options: Personally and without limit, with business and private assets
Jointly and severally with at least one partner
Only up to the capital contributed
questions.correctAnswer: Personally and without limit, with business and private assets

questions.text: Which tax does a sole trader pay on profit?
Which name suits an unregistered sole trader?
options: A freely chosen core name with “GmbH”
First and last name, with an optional activity description
questions.correctAnswer: First and last name, with an optional activity description

questions.text: What applies to profit and loss?
options: The bank receives the profit and the owner bears the loss
The owner keeps the profit and bears the loss alone
Profit is always shared equally with employees
Profit is taxed as corporate income and loss is shared
questions.correctAnswer: The owner keeps the profit and bears the loss alone

questions.text: A sole trader can hire employees.
A sole trader is liable only with business assets, not private assets.
Name two features of a sole proprietorship and one typical challenge.
questions.correctAnswer: For example: one person owns and manages the business; no minimum capital; the owner keeps all profit. Challenge: personal unlimited liability, including private assets.

questions.text: What is the minimum number of partners in an OG?
How are OG partners liable?
options: Personally without limit, directly, jointly and severally
Only with company assets and never personally
Only up to the registered liability amount
Limited to their own capital contribution
questions.correctAnswer: Personally without limit, directly, jointly and severally

questions.text: Who may generally manage and represent an OG?
options: Only the partner with the largest capital share

questions.text: Who has unlimited liability in a KG?
options: Both only up to the liability amount

questions.text: What is the role of a limited partner (Kommanditist)?
options: Liability up to the registered amount, no management, usually control rights
No contribution and no control rights
Unlimited liability and representation like every OG partner
questions.correctAnswer: Liability up to the registered amount, no management, usually control rights

questions.text: Which statement about a silent partnership is correct?
options: It is a contractual stake and is not entered in the commercial register
The silent partner must manage the business alone
The silent partner is listed as a partner in the register
It is a separate legal form with its own legal personality
questions.correctAnswer: It is a contractual stake and is not entered in the commercial register

questions.text: An OG partner signs a contract despite an internal rule that only another partner may sign. What applies externally?
options: The contract is valid only after supervisory-board approval
The contract binds only the signing partner
The contract is generally valid externally
questions.correctAnswer: The contract is generally valid externally

questions.text: An OG and a KG pay income tax themselves on their profits.
A silent partner generally has no right to manage the business.
An OG has failed to repay a EUR 70,000 loan. What may the bank demand from one individual OG partner?
questions.correctAnswer: The bank may demand the full EUR 70,000 from one partner; liability is personal, unlimited, direct, joint and several.

questions.text: What is a GmbH or AG in legal terms?
options: A partnership without its own legal personality
A sole proprietorship with several owners
A legal person with its own legal personality
questions.correctAnswer: A legal person with its own legal personality

questions.text: What is the minimum GmbH share capital, and how much must be paid in cash immediately?
What is the minimum AG share capital, and what portion must be paid at formation?
Who calls the ordinary general meeting of an AG?
Who appoints and supervises the management board?
How is the AG legal reserve calculated before it reaches 10% of share capital?
An AG has EUR 7,000,000 share capital, 70,000 shares and EUR 900,000 profit after corporate tax. The reserve is not yet full. What is the dividend per share after the 5% reserve?
The total tax burden for a GmbH shareholder when profits are distributed is 44.175%.
A GmbH requires minimum share capital of EUR 70,000, with one quarter paid in cash.
Calculate the total tax on EUR 100,000 of GmbH profit when fully distributed, and state what the shareholder keeps.
questions.correctAnswer: Corporate tax: EUR 23,000, leaving EUR 77,000. Capital gains tax: 27.5% of EUR 77,000 = EUR 21,175. Total tax EUR 44,175 (44.175%); the shareholder keeps EUR 55,825.

questions.text: A share has a EUR 2 par value and is issued for EUR 3. What is the premium (Agio) per share?
How is share capital calculated from the number of shares and their par value?
options: Number of shares × par value per share
Number of shares + par value per share
questions.correctAnswer: Number of shares × par value per share

questions.text: Shares may be issued below their par value.
With EUR 3,000,000 share capital, 50,000 shares and EUR 400,000 annual profit (reserve not yet full), what are the dividend per share and dividend percentage after the reserve?
Which statement about shareholder rights and the market price is correct?
options: Subscription rights apply only to board members; each share gives ten votes; the market price always equals par value.
Subscription rights preserve an ownership percentage after a capital increase; each share gives one vote; the market price is set by supply and demand.
Shareholders have no subscription rights; votes depend on profit; the supervisory board sets the market price.
Subscription rights replace dividends; each share gives one vote; the market price equals share capital.
questions.correctAnswer: Subscription rights preserve an ownership percentage after a capital increase; each share gives one vote; the market price is set by supply and demand.
